options.a: Keep a resident safely seated in a wheelchair between activities
options.b: Lift a resident from the floor after a fall by pulling up on the belt
options.c: Provide a secure hold to assist ambulation/transfers
options.d: Pull the resident up in bed by grasping the belt at the back

distractorExplanations.a: Using a gait belt to hold someone in a chair makes it a restraint; it is a transfer and walking aid.
distractorExplanations.b: A fallen resident is assessed by the nurse first and raised with a mechanical lift, not hauled up by a gait belt.
distractorExplanations.d: Moving a resident up in bed uses a lift or draw sheet; gait belts are for transfers and ambulation.

nnaap-cna-readiness-check-adls-safety-00.explanation: Gait belts aid safe mobility; they are not punitive restraints. Use one when appropriate for the resident's condition and care plan.

options.a: Performed past the point of pain to increase joint flexibility
options.b: Performed as ordered, supporting joints, stopping if pain occurs
options.c: Performed quickly with each joint moved 20 times per session
options.d: Performed on the neck for every resident daily to prevent contractures

distractorExplanations.d: Neck ROM is done only when ordered and is often limited to licensed or therapy staff; it is not a daily routine for every resident.
distractorExplanations.a: Range of motion stops at the point of pain or resistance; forcing it can injure the joint.
distractorExplanations.c: ROM is done slowly and smoothly with a few repetitions per joint as ordered, not fast high counts.

options.a: Remove the top linens fully so the bottom sheet is easier to reach
options.b: Have the resident sit in a chair while you change the occupied bed
options.c: Keep the resident covered and roll them toward the open side without rails
options.d: Keep the resident covered for privacy and use side rails per policy

distractorExplanations.a: Leaving the resident uncovered violates privacy and warmth; a bath blanket keeps them covered.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes making an unoccupied bed; an occupied bed is made with the resident in it.
distractorExplanations.c: Rolling toward an unprotected side risks a fall; roll toward a raised rail or a second staff member.

nnaap-cna-readiness-check-adls-safety-01.explanation: Occupied bedmaking maintains safety, dignity, and infection control. Covering the resident protects privacy and warmth. A raised rail or second staff member on the far side keeps the resident safe during turning.

options.a: Check water temperature with the resident's foot before they step in
options.b: Check water temperature and ensure grab bars/nonslip surfaces
options.c: Check that the resident can lock the door for privacy during the shower
options.d: Set the water as hot as the resident prefers, then step out to give privacy

distractorExplanations.a: The NA checks water with a thermometer or the inner wrist; residents may have impaired sensation in the feet.
distractorExplanations.c: A locked door prevents help in an emergency; privacy is protected with curtains and covering instead.
distractorExplanations.d: Water must be safely warm per policy, and an at-risk resident should not be left alone in the shower.

nnaap-cna-readiness-check-adls-safety-01.explanation: Burns and falls are major shower risks. Water should be safely warm when checked. Stay within safety guidelines and do not leave an at-risk resident alone.
